chunks: Faḍālah narrated from Abān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If two parties disagree concerning the pledge, and one of them says, ‘I pledged it for one thousand dirhams,’ while the other says, ‘I pledged it for one hundred dirhams,’ then the one claiming one thousand is asked for proof. If he does not have proof, the one claiming one hundred swears an oath. And if the pledged property is less than what it was pledged for or more, and they disagree concerning the pledge, so one of them says, ‘It is a pledge,’ and the other says, ‘It is a deposit,’ then the one claiming it is a deposit is asked for proof. If he does not have proof, the one claiming it is a pledge swears an oath.

key_terms.الرَّهْنِ: pledged collateral held as security for a debt
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةَ: legal proof or evidence required to support a claim
key_terms.بِأَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ: for one thousand dirhams, the higher claimed amount in the dispute
key_terms.بِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: for one hundred dirhams, the lower claimed amount in the dispute
key_terms.حَلَفَ: swore an oath in the absence of proof
key_terms.وَدِيعَةٌ: a deposited item held in trust rather than as collateral

ai.seo_question: How is a dispute over collateral or a deposit resolved in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for disputes over pledged property and the amount for which it was pledged. It places the burden of proof upon the claimant whose assertion opposes the apparent presumption, and if proof is lacking, the opposing party is made to swear an oath. It also addresses disputes over whether an item is a pledge or a deposit.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4116 - Fadalah narrated from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (as):
"If two parties disagree about the value of collateral (rahn), with one claiming it was pledged for one thousand dirhams and the other claiming it was pledged for one hundred dirhams, the one claiming the higher value must present evidence. If he cannot provide evidence, the one claiming the lower value must take an oath."

"Similarly, if the collateral is worth either less or more than the claimed amount, and they disagree about its status, whether it is collateral (rahn) or a deposit (wadi'ah), the one claiming it is a deposit must present evidence. If he cannot provide evidence, the one claiming it is collateral must take an oath."
